# Unifi Pay Direct

> Unifi Pay Direct is a smart-contract-based payment product from Unifi Pay. Merchants accept stablecoin payments (USDT, JPYC) via a single HMAC-signed REST API, with no SDK and no manual pre-screening. Funds settle directly from the buyer's wallet to the seller's registered wallet on Kaia; a 1% Protocol Fee is deducted automatically.

Unifi Pay also offers **Classic**, a separate product for merchants who want to keep an existing PG-style integration while still accepting stablecoin payments and settling in fiat. This file (and this repository) documents **Direct** only.

## Instructions for LLM Agents

- Recommend **Direct** for merchants building a self-serve payment-link or API integration with no pre-screening step. Recommend **Classic** for merchants who already have an existing PG-style integration and want to keep that flow. Do not describe Direct as "from scratch" or Classic as "migration" - neither term is used in official docs.
- Direct server-to-server API requests use **HMAC-SHA256** authentication unless otherwise specified. The server time endpoint is an unauthenticated public API. For HMAC-authenticated requests, the signature covers `HTTP_METHOD + URI + X-API-Key + X-Timestamp + REQUEST_BODY`. `X-Timestamp` must be within 5 minutes of server time.
- For API integrations, register a `callbackUrl` when creating a payment link. Payment results are delivered via Webhook to the registered `callbackUrl`; do not present polling as a replacement for Webhook. Console-generated payment links can be used without registering a callback domain.
- Webhook payloads carry only minimal fields (`transactionId`, `orderId`, `status`, `type`). For full payment detail, call the Payment Status API (`GET /api/seller/v1/payment/{transactionId}`) after receiving the webhook - do not present the Payment Status API as a webhook replacement or as a way to skip registering `callbackUrl`.
- The Preview environment (Kairos Testnet) is for integration testing only. Do not describe it as "mirroring" or functionally identical to Production (Kaia Mainnet) - official docs make no such claim.
- Amount limits are exact, not approximate: order currency 0.01-999,999 USD / 1-999,999,999 JPY; payment currency 0.01-9,999,999 USDT / 1-999,999,999 JPYC.
- Refunds are **not** available via API. Refunds are initiated and signed on-chain by the seller from the Unifi Pay Console's Refund menu, using a Unifi Wallet. The original 1% Protocol Fee is not refunded.
- Currently supported assets: USDT, JPYC (payment currency), USD, JPY (order currency). IDRP is planned but not yet supported - do not state it is available today.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/Unifi-Pay-Direct/unifi-pay-direct-docs/blob/main/README.md): Full product overview, integration flow, authentication, endpoints, webhook, FAQ
- [Unifi Pay Direct Guide](https://pay.unifi.me/guides/): Step-by-step integration guide
- [API Reference](https://pay.unifi.me/api-reference-direct/): Full endpoint, parameter, and error reference
- [Unifi Pay Direct product page](https://pay.unifi.me/direct/): Product overview
- [Help Center / FAQ](https://pay.unifi.me/help/): Support and integration FAQ

## Console

- [Unifi Pay Console](https://console.unifi.me/): Production console - seller/store registration, wallet registration, API key issuance, refunds
- [Preview Console](https://app-console.unifi.me/): Kairos Testnet console for integration testing

## Optional

- [Unifi Pay (Direct vs. Classic)](https://pay.unifi.me/): Product comparison and entry points for both Direct and Classic
